stories.title: Nepra raises industrial tariff to Rs25.30 per unit, despite dissent
summary: Interestingly, Nepra Chairman Waseem Mukhtar fully endorsed the written arguments and positions taken by the dissenting members but subsequently exercised his special casting vote to approve the revised rate of Rs25.30 per unit instead of retaining the existing rate of Rs22.98.

The dissenting members argued that compliance with the federal cabinet’s decision and Nepra’s own directives required a reassessment of the existing rate of Rs22.98 per unit to determine whether it should be retained, revised or suspended.
The two members, therefore, recommended the temporary suspension of the tariff package rather than choosing the proposed rate of Rs25.30 or above per unit.

stories.title: Bavaria’s speaker tipped to become Germany’s first woman president
summary: Aigner, 61, now the speaker of the southern state’s regional assembly, would replace outgoing President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a Social Democrat, in the largely ceremonial post.
Aigner belongs to the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of the centre-right CDU of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is supporting the choice of Aigner, the party sources said.
Aigner’s political appeal owes much to a trademark Bavarian warmth, and her appearances in a traditional dirndl dress at beer festivals have made her a familiar figure across the state.

stories.title: SC calls for scrutiny of illegal power connections
summary: Petitioner Ali Asghar Khokhar, a resident of Khuhawar Street, Larkana, had filed a criminal petition before the SC seeking cancellation of bail granted to respondent Anwar Ali Kori by the Sindh High Court’s Larkana circuit bench on Oct 20, 2025.

The allegation was that the co-accused, including Wapda officials and the respondent, were supplying electricity to people in their shops by laying a special line from the disposal phase line and running an electric wire over the complainant’s shops.
Furthermore, the high court’s order also reflected the IO’s statement that the respondent had no contact with Wapda officials.

stories.title: Trump promotes Stephen Miller to chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
summary: US President Donald Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller on Friday, elevating the architect of some of his toughest domestic policies to run the White House after Republicans lost control of Congress in this week’s midterm elections.
White House officials told Reuters that Miller’s selection suggests Trump will take an aggressive approach to domestic policy and politics.

Since Trump’s return to the White House in 2025, Miller has officially been deputy chief of staff under Wiles, but he wielded outsize influence across much of Trump’s domestic agenda and has had the ear of the president.

stories.title: Banks, utilities among services put on alert against AI-enabled cyberthreats
summary: The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (NCERT) has warned of an increased use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automated bots to carry out credential-based and coordinated cyberattacks, noting that critical infrastructure and financial services are at particular risk.

Threat indicators The advisory listed anomalies which may indicate a potential cyberattack targeting financial institutions, such as frequent automated login attempts, repeated authentication failures, and unusual application programming interface (API) requests.
Recommendations NCERT recommended that financial institutions check their core banking security, APIs, third-party integrations, payment gateways and digital banking applications.

stories.title: Activists breach Microsoft data centre construction site as protests spread in Europe
summary: Protesters broke into the construction site of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam on Friday at the start of two days of rallies that are part of a growing global backlash over the rapid build-out of computing power needed for AI.

Activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday, according to the “Stop Dirty Data Centres” coalition, which is rallying environmental groups and digital rights campaigns behind calls to pause large-scale construction.
The Netherlands has about 200 data centres either planned, under construction or in operation.

stories.title: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO
summary: Mahmood was appointed on Sep 23 as the first secretary general of the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

The Makkah Defence Alliance has garnered particular attention as Saudi Arabia faces attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, including a deadly strike that closed Riyadh’s international airport for two weeks last month.

Pakistan, others actively making efforts for peace in Middle East In his briefing, Khan also touched upon the crisis in the Gulf, saying that Pakistan would continue its efforts to facilitate dialogue in the conflict involving Iran and the United States.

stories.title: Newsroom bomb threats follow escalating European flight hoaxes
summary: Newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria received emailed bomb threats on Friday from a purported “Mikhail Andropov”, claiming responsibility for a widening wave of hoax threats disrupting passenger flights across Europe.

On Friday, an Italian airport authority source said a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome had been diverted to Venice but, despite more than a dozen hoax threats, overall there was far less direct disruption to air travel.

EU commissioner says Russia is often to blame for attacks Security experts said on Thursday that the threats had the hallmarks of a coordinated “hybrid attack”, although it was always possible that individuals were issuing copycat threats or acting on personal grievances.

stories.title: CDF Munir, Sudan's interior minister discuss avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation: ISPR
summary: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Sudan’s Interior Minister Lieutenant General (Police) Babiker Samra Mustafa Ali on Friday discussed avenues to enhance bilateral cooperation between their countries.
CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s desire to “further deepen bilateral engagement with Sudan and underscored the importance of close cooperation in addressing shared security challenges”.
He underscored the importance Pakistan attached to its relations with Sudan and its commitment to further strengthening the brotherly ties between the two countries.

stories.title: Bilawal urges govt to stop 'fighting everyone'
summary: Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday urged the federal government and political parties to set aside their differences and engage all political, social and provincial stakeholders to tackle the economic crisis.

Meanwhile, Bilawal directed the government to ensure timely completion and quality execution of key infrastructure projects across Larkana division, including a revamped water and sewerage system for Larkana city and a new wholesale fruit and vegetable market.
The meeting reviewed progress on three major initiatives: the water supply and drainage system in Larkana, relocation of its fruit and vegetable market, and a sewerage scheme in Shahdadkot.

stories.title: PM seeks roadmap for cashless economy
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday directed the relevant authorities to prepare a clear roadmap, with specific timelines and targets, for establishing a fully digital payment system across the country as the government steps up efforts to promote a cashless economy.

Chairing a high-level meeting in Islamabad to review progress on the government's cashless economy initiative, the prime minister said promoting digital payments was among the government's top priorities, adding that positive results had started to emerge.

The prime minister called for promoting digital transactions between consumers and merchants through the government's Raast QR Code initiative, saying it was helping advance the vision of a cashless economy.

stories.title: Punjab govt endorses Asif's 'conspiracy' remark
summary: Incensed by the claim, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz served a Rs5 billion defamation notice on Salik and the private news channel on November 3 over the allegations, demanding an unconditional apology, retraction of the statements and damages.

Commenting on the controversy on X, PML-N stalwart and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on November 4 said the only way to interpret Salik's statement was to see it as a political move to create more space for his party in the Centre and Punjab by targeting CM Maryam's government.
PML-Q spokesperson Ghulam Mustafa Malik, however, dismissed the suggestion of a conspiracy against the Punjab government, saying that even Khawaja Asif had endorsed the corruption allegations.

stories.title: Pakistan says US midterm results won't unravel ties
summary: Meanwhile, the Foreign Office reiterated Pakistan's willingness to facilitate Indian religious pilgrims despite the strained relations between the two neighbouring countries.
Haider said Pakistan had issued 9,318 visas to Indian religious pilgrims in 2025, including 9,070 Sikh pilgrims and 248 Hindu pilgrims.
Haider added that Pakistan had not imposed a visa ban on Indian nationals and would continue facilitating visits to religious sites under the existing arrangements.

stories.title: Iran holds firm on seven demands
summary: Senior security official Mohsen Rezaei had also warned that Iran would neither reopen the Strait of Hormuz nor negotiate without its seven conditions.
In Bahrain, authorities have intensified a crackdown on clerics accused of promoting allegiance to Iran.
Bahrain's security chief Tariq Al Hassan said the authorities were confronting an ideology that placed obedience to Iran's leadership above national sovereignty.

stories.title: Israeli opp closes in on Netanyahu ouster
summary: Israel's opposition on Friday reported progress in efforts to end Benjamin Netanyahu's rule after a key opposition leader softened his opposition to an alliance with ultra-Orthodox parties, potentially opening a path out of the country's post-election political deadlock.

Former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main rival, said negotiations had produced significant breakthroughs, expressing confidence that President Isaac Herzog would nominate him to form a government when he announces his decision on Sunday.

The breakthrough came after opposition leader Avigdor Liberman, who had campaigned against exemptions from military service for ultra-Orthodox Jews, signalled his willingness to negotiate with their political representatives.

stories.title: Newsroom bomb threats add to Euro flight hoaxes
summary: A widening wave of hoax bomb threats targeting passenger flights and news organisations disrupted air travel across Europe for a third consecutive day on Friday, prompting evacuations, flight diversions and military escorts, although no explosives were found.
Reuters could not establish the sender's identity or determine whether the emails originated from the same source as threats affecting dozens of flights since Tuesday.
Meanwhile, Vladislav Pozdniakov, founder of Russia's banned far-right misogynist movement Male State, denied involvement in the threats.

stories.title: FBI arrests Meghan Markle's father
summary: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Prince Harry's wife, Meghan Markle, was arrested in Florida on Friday over alleged possession of images of child sexual abuse, British and US media reported.
The Daily Mail, quoting an unidentified source, said Markle was arrested on charges of possession of child sexual abuse material.
Meghan Markle said last month that she was "deeply distressed" by accusations that her father possessed images of child sexual abuse.

stories.title: Kashmiris observe Jammu Martyrs Day
summary: A public holiday was observed across Azad Jammu and Kashmir to facilitate people in participating in commemorative activities and paying tribute to the martyrs.

According to a report published in the London-based newspaper The Times on August 10, 1948, Dogra forces systematically liquidated over 237,000 Muslims, while nearly 500,000 were forced to migrate toward Pakistan and Azad Kashmir.

Historians and analysts regard this as one of the largest and fastest single massacres following World War II, laying historical roots that connect directly to ongoing policies in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK).

stories.title: Meghan Markle's estranged father arrested for child pornography possession: US authorities
summary: Thomas Markle, father of Prince Harry’s wife Meghan Markle, has been arrested for possessing child pornography, the US Justice Department said on Friday.
Authorities in the Philippines, where Markle had previously lived for some time, began investigating him last month over the allegations.

British tabloid The Sun reported last month that Markle’s son, Thomas Markle Jr, had discovered the child sex abuse images while going through boxes found in his father’s former home in the Philippines.

stories.title: AI tools increase cyberattack risks
summary: It warned that banks could face attacks targeting core banking systems, digital banking platforms, payment systems and customer-facing applications.

Critical infrastructure could also be exposed through vulnerabilities in third-party service providers, connected internet of things (IoT) devices, industrial control systems and insecure remote access, the advisory said.
NCERT urged financial institutions to review the security of core banking systems, APIs, third-party integrations, payment gateways and digital banking applications.

stories.title: Pakistan, UK to strengthen anti-drug cooperation
summary: During the meeting, both countries agreed to strengthen cooperation in counterterrorism, drug control, cybercrime, immigration, identity management through NADRA, coast guard operations and training programmes.
He said Pakistan and the United Kingdom already had strong cooperation in several areas and wanted to expand it further.
The two sides also agreed to convene a meeting of the working group established between the interior ministries of Pakistan and the United Kingdom soon.

stories.title: NADRA officer gunned down in Peshawar
summary: A senior official of the National Database Registration Authority (NADRA) was gunned down outside his office in Peshawar on Friday morning in an apparent case of targeted killing.
According to police, the NADRA official died on the spot as the attackers fled the scene unchallenged.
According to some officials, the police had found images of the assailants and had also shared them with NADRA for identification.

stories.title: Bilawal urges federal govt to engage all political forces instead of ‘fighting everyone’
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Friday urged the PML-N-led federal government to engage all political and social stakeholders rather than “fighting everyone”.
Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

stories.title: Trade gap widens 16% to $14.6b
summary: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) reported on Friday that the gap between imports and exports widened to $14.6 billion during July to October, $2 billion or 16% more than the same period last year.
The PBS said cumulative exports during July to October increased to $11.4 billion, a rise of just $890 million or 8.5% over the same period last year.
The government has now projected goods exports of $34 billion this fiscal year, against $30.8 billion last year.

stories.title: Turkish seismic vessel due in Karachi
summary: A Turkish seismic vessel will arrive in Karachi between November 17 and 20, 2026, reviving Pakistan's offshore exploration efforts after nearly two decades, Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik said while chairing a meeting to review preparations for its arrival.

The meeting reviewed operational, logistical, maritime, security and interdepartmental arrangements for the vessel's arrival and the commencement of the offshore exploration campaign to build Pakistan's energy security.
Pakistan's offshore exploration has been largely dormant for nearly two decades, and officials said the arrival would also strengthen bilateral energy cooperation between the two countries.

stories.title: Ministry to devise tobacco deregulation system
summary: The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC), in a recent meeting, agreed with the price fixing proposal approved by the Pakistan Tobacco Board (PTB), stressing that it was the need of the hour to chalk out an exit strategy for the federal government from price fixation.

The food security ministry pointed out that a summary on the minimum indicative price of tobacco crop (2026) and the revision in tobacco cess rates for financial year 2026-27 had been presented to the ECC in its meeting held on September 7, 2026.

Keeping in view the prevailing economic conditions and in the best interest of tobacco growers, the Ministry of Food Security proposed that MIPs and cess rates notified for the previous year (2025) may be maintained for the 2026 crop.

stories.title: Online ship, boat registration begins
summary: Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry on Friday announced that the online ship and boat registration system had become operational, enabling vessel owners to submit registration applications electronically without visiting government offices.
In a statement, the minister said the ship and boat registration modules were now fully accessible for online applications following the completion of necessary measures.
The ministry is also working to introduce online payments to further facilitate the applicants.

stories.title: No to wars
summary: A presidential statement from Islamabad - which called on member states to "continue diplomatic engagement even after the outbreak of armed conflicts" - was recognised as the way forward.
The statement, titled "The Role of Diplomacy during Active Hostilities", could not have come at a more opportune moment, as the world sits on tenterhooks amid quasi-peace and uncertainty.
It is a pity that the US spent over $8 trillion on wars and conflicts in the post-9/11 era.

stories.title: Modern child labour!
summary: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency's (NCCIA) raid on a call centre on Sharea Faisal, Karachi for alleged cyber fraud, which led to the arrest of 273 employees, has drawn increased attention to the employment structure of call centres in general.
Ignorance is no excuse, and it is also unlikely, as most people can quickly summarise from their job descriptions and pay scales whether or not their employer is on the up and up.
The NCCIA has suggested it would charge the parents of any underage employees, a move that we support.

stories.title: Fighting potential
summary: Pakistan's sporting potential extends well beyond cricket, although opportunities to recognise and develop talent in other disciplines remain limited.
Young people are increasingly taking up the discipline, while domestic competitions and privately organised events are creating opportunities for aspiring fighters to test their abilities.
Pakistan has also demonstrated its capabilities internationally, having hosted the IMMAF Asian Championships in Lahore in 2024 and produced medal-winning athletes at subsequent competitions.

stories.title: Elon Musk's futuristic Cybertruck rolls toward exit
summary: Tesla fans lamented the departure of the Cybertruck on X, the social media platform Musk owns, but the tycoon reassured them that the Cybertruck fleet “will be around for a long time”.
As US demand slumped, Tesla began selling the truck abroad, starting deliveries in South Korea in November 2025 and in the United Arab Emirates in January.
Tesla began production at the Texas plant in April and started offering paid Cybercab rides in Austin in September through its existing Robotaxi service.

stories.title: Turkish vessel to arrive in Karachi between Nov 17-20 to begin offshore oil, gas exploration
summary: ISLAMABAD: A Turkish seismic vessel will arrive in Karachi between November 17 and 20 to begin offshore oil and gas exploration, the Petroleum Division said on Friday.

The announcement followed a meeting between Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and relevant agencies to review preparations and arrangements for the arrival of the seismic vessel of Turkish Petroleum Offshore Company (TPOC) in Pakistan.

The meeting reviewed operational, logistical, maritime, security and interdepartmental arrangements for the vessel’s arrival and commencement of the offshore exploration campaign to build Pakistan’s energy security.

stories.title: Usman Khan’s unbeaten century powers Pakistan to emphatic win over UAE in U-19 Asia Cup
summary: Usman led the charge with an unbeaten 139 off 120 balls, hitting 21 fours and a six.
Qadir remained unbeaten on 20 off 19 deliveries, striking a four and a six.
UAE managed 224 in their allotted 50 overs, with Noorullah Ayobi leading the scoring with a brisk 70 off 55 balls, including three fours and six sixes.

stories.title: EU charges TikTok over harmful algorithmic 'rabbit hole' effects, tells it to change 'For You' feed
summary: It said the platform should change the design of its ‘For You’ feed algorithm and should rely more on users’ explicit preferences, increase the accessibility and usability of user controls and regularly test its algorithm, among other changes.
Even when users tell TikTok they do not like certain content, the platform’s algorithm continues to suggest similar videos.
In its preliminary findings, the EU said TikTok did not “adequately assess” how its recommendation algorithm put users’ wellbeing at risk.

stories.title: CDF Munir, Sudan's interior minister pledge to deepen security and counterterrorism cooperation
summary: Earlier in the day, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar also met Sudan's interior minister, the Foreign Office said in a statement.
The prime minister warmly welcomed the visiting dignitary and said Pakistan attached great importance to its longstanding and fraternal relations with Sudan.

The visiting minister appreciated Pakistan's support at international forums for efforts to restore peace and security in Sudan and praised its role in promoting regional peace and mediation, the statement said.

stories.title: How China's clean-tech machine is reshaping the global climate fight
summary: The $132bn figure derived by Reuters for China’s global climate contribution also includes an estimated $40 billion of Chinese foreign direct investment into clean-technology projects in developing countries.

That brings China’s contribution to nearly equal to the $137bn in climate finance that wealthy nations provided to poorer ones in 2024 under their UN climate pledges, according to the most recent figures provided by the OECD.
Nearly two thirds of China’s exports of solar panels, and the cells needed to make them, went to the developing world last year, according to Reuters analysis of customs data.
